findings.title: Non-snapshot entries inflate file-history churn and rework scores
findings.what: The parser selects every directory entry whose name ends in @v2 without checking Dirent.isFile(). It computes churn before stat validation, and statSync follows symlinks. Consequently, an @v2 directory or symlink is counted as a checkpoint, while an entry whose stat fails still remains in churn whenever another entry has a valid mtime. The emitted churn, burstRate, and reworkScore therefore need not be supported by actual snapshot files.
findings.fix: Filter sessionEntries to regular files before counting, and build churn and mtimes from the same successfully validated entries; use lstat or the existing Dirent type to reject symlinks and directories.
findings.acceptance: Add regression cases containing a directory named fake@v2, a symlink named link@v2, and an unreadable or vanished entry alongside one valid snapshot. parseFileHistoryDir must count only the valid regular snapshot, and its churn, spanMin, burstRate, and reworkScore must derive from that same accepted set.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial second pass re-read src/lib/parse-file-history.ts:109-132 and src/lib/parse-file-history.test.ts:116-168 at the specified baseline. Line 114 retains only names and suffixes, line 116 counts them before stat results are filtered at lines 120-126, and the existing tests create only regular files, so no baseline guard rejects or covers non-regular and failed-stat entries.
